introduction-security-in-depth.core: Defence in depth layers independent controls so no single failure exposes you: identity (IAM), network (security groups, WAF, Shield), data (KMS encryption, Macie discovery) and detection (GuardDuty, Security Hub). Each layer assumes the others might fail.

first_principles.problem: A single misconfigured security group exposes a database because nothing else stood in the way.
derivation: **Prevent** at identity, network and application layers.

analogy.title: A castle's defences
analogy.story: Moat, walls, gatehouse, guards and a locked keep. Breaching one doesn't give you the crown.
analogy.breaks: Castles face one direction of attack; cloud attacks come from insiders and supply chains too.

example.title: Layered protection of a database
flow: Private subnet + SG from app only

check.q: Why add detection when you already have prevention?
check.a: Prevention eventually fails; detection catches attacks that slip through so you can respond.

kms-the-core-of-encryption.core: KMS manages keys in HSMs and never exports key material. Services use envelope encryption: KMS generates a data key, the service encrypts data with it, and stores the data key encrypted under your KMS key. Key policies (plus IAM and grants) control who can use keys, and CloudTrail logs every use.

first_principles.problem: Encryption keys stored alongside data in config files are stolen with the data.
truths: Keys must be protected separately from data.
Encrypting large data directly with a remote key is slow.
derivation: **Key policy** is the primary access control.

analogy.title: A master key in a bank vault that locks the small keys
analogy.story: You carry small keys around; the master that locks them never leaves the vault.
analogy.breaks: Bank masters can be copied by locksmiths; KMS key material never leaves the HSMs.

example.title: Envelope encryption
flow: Encrypt file locally with plaintext key, discard it
Store encrypted key with the file
Decrypt: KMS Decrypt(encrypted key) → plaintext key

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Data keys usable only via KMS permission.

example.outcome: keys separated from data, all use logged.

check.q: Why use envelope encryption instead of encrypting data directly with KMS?
check.a: KMS Encrypt has a 4 KB limit and network latency; data keys encrypt bulk data locally while KMS protects the data key.

kms-multi-region-keys.core: Multi-Region keys are sets of KMS keys in different regions sharing the same key ID and key material, so data encrypted in one region can be decrypted in another without a cross-region call or re-encryption. Each replica has its own key policy. They suit global tables, DR and client-side encryption across regions.

first_principles.problem: Encrypted data replicated to a DR region can't be decrypted without calling the source region's KMS, which might be down.
derivation: Use for **DynamoDB global tables, S3 replication, client-side encryption**.
Avoid where **strict regional isolation** is required.

analogy.title: Identical master keys kept in branch vaults in two cities
analogy.story: Either branch can open boxes locked in the other.
analogy.breaks: Physical key copies drift; multi-Region keys sync rotation automatically.

code.text:
aws kms create-key --multi-region --description app-data
aws kms replicate-key --key-id mrk-1234abcd --replica-region eu-west-1

guardduty-the-intelligent-watchdog.core: GuardDuty continuously analyses CloudTrail management and data events, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs and optional sources (EKS audit logs, runtime monitoring, S3, RDS login activity, Lambda network) using threat intelligence and ML to flag compromised credentials, crypto-mining, reconnaissance and data exfiltration. No agents are needed for the core sources.

first_principles.problem: Stolen credentials mine cryptocurrency for days before anyone notices the bill.
truths: Humans can't read every log line.
derivation: Turn on **protection plans** (S3, EKS, runtime, RDS).

analogy.title: A guard dog that knows every burglar's scent
analogy.story: It patrols constantly and barks at unusual behaviour.
analogy.breaks: Dogs sleep; GuardDuty runs continuously but may still miss novel attacks.

example.title: Automated response
flow: Revoke role sessions, isolate instance SG

check.q: Does GuardDuty need agents to analyse VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs?
check.a: No; it reads those independently without agents (agents are only for runtime monitoring).

waf-vs-shield-the-shield-and-the-sword.core: AWS WAF inspects HTTP(S) requests at CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway and AppSync, blocking SQL injection, XSS, bad bots and abusive IPs with managed and custom rules and rate limits (layer 7). Shield Standard protects all customers from common layer 3/4 DDoS automatically. Shield Advanced adds enhanced detection, the DDoS response team and cost protection.

first_principles.problem: A login endpoint is hammered by credential stuffing while a volumetric DDoS targets the site.
truths: Application attacks look like valid HTTP.
derivation: Use **AWS Managed Rules** (core, SQLi, known bad inputs, bot control).

analogy.title: A club bouncer versus flood barriers
analogy.story: The bouncer checks each guest's behaviour; the barriers hold back the flood.
analogy.breaks: Bouncers judge intent; WAF rules match patterns and can produce false positives.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: IPs over 100 login requests/5 min blocked.

check.q: Which layer does Shield Standard protect?
check.a: Network and transport layers (L3/L4) against common DDoS attacks.

macie-finding-the-needle-in-the-haystack.core: Macie inventories S3 buckets (encryption, public access, sharing) and uses managed and custom data identifiers plus ML to discover sensitive data like PII, credentials and financial data in objects. Automated discovery samples continuously; findings flow to Security Hub and EventBridge.

first_principles.problem: Nobody knows which of 4,000 buckets contain customer passport scans.
truths: Compliance requires knowing where PII lives.

analogy.title: A metal detector sweeping a beach
analogy.story: It finds the valuable or dangerous items buried in tons of sand.
analogy.breaks: Metal detectors find metal only; Macie needs identifiers for each data type you care about.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Exposure closed before an audit or breach.

check.a: S3 bucket configurations and object contents for sensitive data like PII.
